# go-modern-range-over-int

**Since:** Go 1.22

## Summary

Use for i := range n when iterating from 0 to n-1.

## Details

Ranging over an integer is the concise Go 1.22 form for zero-based count loops.
Keep a traditional for loop when you need a non-zero start, custom step, or changing bound.

## Examples

### Before

```go
for i := 0; i < len(items); i++ {
  process(items[i])
}
```

### After

```go
for i := range len(items) {
  process(items[i])
}
```

Source: [https://github.com/JetBrains/go-modern-guidelines/blob/main/internal/guidelines/guidelines.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/go-modern-guidelines/blob/main/internal/guidelines/guidelines.json)
